title: Complete Classification of Positive-Slope Relative-Bound Equiangular Line Families, Exact Fixed-Angle Thresholds, and Consecutive-Dimension Extensions
abstract: Djaljapayan, Liao, and Yu (arXiv:2611.34855v1, Section 5) combine repeated-Seidel-block constructions with the Bukh-Cox coherence bound to establish exact fixed-angle values N_{1/q}(d) = d + k on linearly growing intervals of consecutive dimensions for k = 7 (all odd q >= 319) and k = 23 (all odd q >= 5599), together with a single-dimension quadratic-irrational family from symmetric conference matrices (Theorem 5.2) and two isolated values at cosine 1/7 (Proposition 5.3). We systematically complete and sharpen every component of that program. First (Theorem 1), we prove an exact linear-in-a classification theorem showing that among all nontrivial relative-bound two-eigenvalue equiangular seeds (k, M, a) (2 <= k <= a^2 - 2, M <= k(k+1)/2), positive Bukh-Cox interval slope L_k > M/b holds if and only if k in {3, 5, 6, 7} for a = 3 and exclusively k in {a^2 - 3, a^2 - 2} for every odd a >= 5; moreover, the submaximal branch k = a^2 - 3 always yields an exact rational Bukh-Cox constant L_{a^2-3} = (a^2-2)(a+1)/((a-1)(a+2)) and exact rational slope a(a+1)/((a-1)(a+2)(a^2+a-3)). Second (Theorem 2), by proving the exact alternating-character eigenvalue range lambda_alt(A) in {-3, -2, -1, 0, 1} for every even-order circulant A (sharpening Q - 2r to Q - 6), replacing the crude r < t bound with r <= b - 1, and constructing explicit {+-1}^M seed eigenvectors S v = -a v that enable odd-t block repetitions with constant Schur ratio rho = k/a, we obtain four new infinite fixed-angle families missed in arXiv:2611.34855v1 -- Tetrahedron k = 3 (q >= 7), Petersen k = 5 (q >= 155; q >= 11 for q = 3 mod 4), Clebsch k = 6 (q >= 161; q >= 89 for q = 1 mod 4), and Higman-Sims k = 22 (q >= 8643) -- while sharpening both existing thresholds (k = 7: 319 -> 245, and 125 for q = 1 mod 4; k = 23: 5599 -> 5267) and uncovering exact zero-gap adjacent-dimension contact d_+^(6) + 1 = d_-^(7) (10 | Q) and d_+^(22) + 1 = d_-^(23) (112 | Q, with single-point +2 jump for all 56 | Q). Third (Theorem 3), we upgrade Theorem 5.2 from a single dimension d = mt - m/2 to an entire consecutive interval of length (sqrt(m^2 + 2m) - m)t + O(1) for every even t >= 2, generalize Proposition 5.3 to infinite s in {2, 3} relative-bound block windows for every odd q >= 5 (catching exact Pell jumps at (q, d) = (15, 25) and (35, 49)), and prove an exact s >= 4 impossibility barrier for all nontrivial (s >= 2) block constructions. All 18 core algebraic theorems are formally verified in constructive Lean 4.35.0 (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 custom axioms) and backed by 16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates and 56 adversarial tests.
